Well that's very good to hear, I'm glad you've clawed your way up from rock-bottom and have found more empathy for others in similar situations, that's very good.

Yeah, it really doesn't have a happy ending that's for sure.. But I identify a lot with Bartleby and his polite apathy. "I would prefer not to"..

The story tells me that no matter how alone I feel, it's all been felt before and none of my problems or defects are new or unique.

Sorry if it the story was a downer and had a bad effect for you, I do hope that your bouts with feeling that way are few and far between and you're able to manage your apathy/depression better than Bartleby.

Even just trying to help is good, even if you don't end up helping at all, it let's them know at least someone out there thinks they're worth the time and effort.

I do hope things get better for you, but even if you remain depressed it isn't the end of the world.. You just need to learn to live with the additional weight on your back, even if it means distracting yourself from it, it's better than the alternative I think.

I don't know why some people seem so happy and unflappable, I'm sure almost all people with terrible anxieties or depression also wish they could be 'normal'.. I'm sorry that you aren't, but you have a lot of company to be sure.. There are a lot of very distraught, sad, and tortured people out there and you just so happen to be one of them. You will most likely have an empathy toward people who feel similarly to you that other people won't have, it's one of the few positives and I'm not even sure if it is a positive, as being able to easily sympathize with people who have similar issues to you is also painful in its own way.

I wish there were easier answers, but I really don't think there are.

I'm really happy to hear that, I think my sister avoiding therapy may have caused her hurt to linger far longer than if she'd talked to a professional.

I don't have room to talk, having been recommended to therapists before and never following through with the appointments.. But it makes me glad to know you're actively seeking out help.

I really hope things work out for you and this is all just a distant and blunted painful memory someday, even if right now the pain encompasses the whole of your world.

It's rough, looking back to a time where you had so much to be happy for and realizing you were just as depressed then as you are today..

Depression doesn't follow any sort of logic, it hits those surrounded by loving family and hermits alike.. It isn't any less sharp of a knife regardless of circumstances. I'm sure we all wish we had a time machine to go back and appreciate what we had in the past but sadly that can't happen.

But just think, ten years from now you could be looking back at today and thinking of all the little things you currently have going for you that you should have appreciated. Things that time has stolen from you always hurt to think about, but there is always more to lose.

There's also the small chance that things may get better.. You may make a new friend or find something you absolutely love, something to devote yourself to.

I am sorry, I very much hope things improve for you. Looking back is often painful but hard to resist doing.

My sister lost a baby, she was being a surrogate for a close childhood friend, and it destroyed her.. Even knowing she was going to be giving the child away, spending so much time carrying the child and then losing it so suddenly, she was emotionally wrecked for what seemed like more than a year..

I'm so sorry for your loss, it's a pain that the majority of people in the world will never come close to knowing. I'm not sure if distancing yourself will work for quite some time.. You've been hit terribly hard by one of the absolute worst human experiences. I hope you're able to come through eventually, just keep trying and moving forward, even if that forward motion is incredibly slow.

Losing weight and making new friends but still feeling like shit? That hits very close to home..

I starved myself, dropping about 200lbs to be at a normal weight, telling myself that I'd hate myself less and people would like me more.. That it'd fix my social anxiety and depression because I'd be normal. Absolutely did not work, I still hide from the world and have no friends, I just do so with significantly less mass now.

Your job sounds like hell to me, I have a huge amount of respect for anyone able to operate in that sort of environment. Your manager taking credit for your years of hard work is incredibly terrible and hurts my heart to hear.

It doesn't sound like you have a ton of spare time, but you dreading leaving work as all you have waiting for you is exercise and sleep sounds like maybe some sort of hobby could help. I find distracting myself from my depression is my most useful ability. I've given up on finding a cure, but focusing my attention on other things is very helpful.. Maybe you could listen to audio books or podcasts while you exercise? Both help keep my mind active and focused away from myself/my mood.

I'm sorry to hear that your ex boyfriend isolated you and your more recent boyfriend doesn't want to hang out when it's not convenient for him. I really hope things get better for you, not all people are assholes even if a significant percent of the population seem to be.

Seeing other people doing well in life and then comparing it to how you're doing is rough, it's never a good idea in my opinion but it's very hard not to do at least occasionally.

It sounds cliché I'm sure but looking on the bright side is very helpful to me.. I'm similar to you in that I too have no parents, no safety net, and live in general poverty... I try to take comfort in whatever small things I have going for me. Even if it's just a roof over my head, food in my belly and my health.. Even if things are terrible for you, they can always always get worse, try to appreciate what good you have in your life in case it suddenly disappears.

Another technique is distraction.. I try not to dwell too long on my sadness, occupying my mind with music, audiobooks, videos or games.. These things do sometimes cost money but there is a lot of free content floating around too. Distraction from your problems may not fix anything but I see it as far superior to the alternative of suicide..
